items.title: BCCK named official venue for national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebrations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) in Sarawak has been officially named the venue for the national-level Malaysia Day celebrations on Sept 16. The decision to hold the main celebration indoors was made to provide a climate-controlled and safe environment for dignitaries and cultural troupes, in view of the current haze affecting parts of Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia. Information Department (JAPEN) Cyber Media Division assistant director Yumna Baharuddin said Sarawak's selection as host aligns with the 2020 Cabinet decision to implement a rotational system between Sarawak, Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia.

items.title: Great Eastern targets affluent customers with new offerings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Great Eastern Life Assurance (Malaysia) Bhd has launched Great Prestige, a dedicated proposition for affluent customers, alongside the unveiling of the Great Prestige Suite at Prince Court Medical Centre, Malaysia's first dedicated premium insurance suite within a medical centre. Great Prestige is designed to support affluent customers as their financial priorities evolve over time while the Great Prestige Suite brings together key elements of the insurance onboarding process in one dedicated environment. These include Prestige Heritage Global, Prestige Heritage Index and Prestige Wealth Index.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Anak Krakatau ash could reach Malaysia, but risk remains low
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The risk of volcanic ash from Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau reaching Malaysia is currently low, although changes in wind direction and speed as well as possible further eruptions could affect its movement, MetMalaysia said today. “Information from global Volcanic Ash Advisory Centres (VAACs) also allows any potential movement of the ash into Malaysian airspace to be identified and communicated to the public promptly,” he said. Earlier, media reports said continued eruptions from Anak Krakatau since Friday had spread volcanic ash and prompted six airports to suspend flight operations.

items.title: After child mauled, Johor orders operation to capture five stray dogs
items.summary: Pix: Najmi Nor'Azam JOHOR BARU: Johor has ordered a major operation to track down and capture five stray dogs that mauled a two-year-old girl in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat. State Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khaled said the dogs must be captured and tested for rabies, with the operation to be intensified for at least a week. Fared said the operation involved the Batu Pahat district office, Veterinary Services Department (DVS) and police.

items.title: PISA 2025: Malaysia improves in Science, Reading but slips in Mathematics
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia recorded encouraging improvements in the Science and Reading literacy domains under the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2025. Results from the triennial PISA study showed Science literacy rose three points to 419, while Reading literacy increased five points to 393 compared with the PISA 2022 report. However, the average score for Mathematics literacy declined by 11 points to 397 compared with the performance recorded three years ago.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Malaysia could see temperatures hit 40°C from January to May 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysia could experience extreme heat and dry weather from January to May next year, with temperatures in some areas potentially reaching 40°C as a very strong El Nino, or Super El Nino, is expected to develop towards the end of this year. He said past meteorological records showed that very strong El Nino episodes were often associated with higher temperatures, dry weather and a serious risk of haze, similar to conditions currently affecting the country. Mohd Hisham said there was about a 70 per cent probability that the intensity of the current El Nino would exceed the strength of any El Nino episode recorded since 1950.

items.title: Nepalis mark a year since deadly protests that toppled government
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Dozens of young people congregated at Nepal's burnt-out parliament building on Tuesday to mark the anniversary of deadly anti-corruption protests that toppled the former government. The unrest caused the deaths of 76 people and the torching of the parliament building in the capital Kathmandu, as well as the prime minister's office and other government buildings. Banners bearing photos of people killed in the protests were hung in the parliament grounds.

items.title: Dismembered body case: Senior citizen's murder charge transferred to High Court
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The magistrate's court today ordered the case of a senior citizen charged with murdering a woman whose dismembered body was found to be transferred to the High Court. Magistrate Dzul Elmy Yunus made the order after allowing the prosecution's application to transfer the case involving Piluta Samad, 72. The prosecution informed the court that it had received instructions to transfer the case to the High Court here.

items.title: 5.2-magnitude earthquake hits Indonesia's Flores region
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A moderate earthquake measuring 5.2 on the Richter scale occurred in the Flores region of Indonesia at 12.40pm today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said in a statement that the earthquake was detected at coordinates 8.1 degrees South and 120.8 degrees East, about 240 kilometres (km) east of Bima, Indonesia. The earthquake occurred at a depth of 34km.

items.title: Senior medical officer in Melaka remanded over RM1.5m knee implant supply probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — A senior medical officer has been remanded for five days to assist a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into alleged abuse of position involving the supply of knee implants worth about RM1.5 million. The remand order for the man, in his 50s, was issued by Ayer Keroh Magistrate Sharda Shienha Mohd Suleiman at the Ayer Keroh Magistrates’ Court in Melaka this morning, Harian Metro reported. The public servant has been remanded until September 12 after MACC applied for the order to facilitate further investigations.

items.title: Thieves steal three paintings from Renoir Museum on French Riviera
items.summary: PARIS: Thieves stole three paintings from the Renoir Museum on the French Riviera early on Tuesday, the local mayor said. The raiders broke into the museum a little before 6am and took four paintings, Cagnes-sur-Mer mayor Bryan Masson said on his Facebook page. "Attacking the Renoir museum is attacking a part of the history and heritage of Cagnes-sur-Mer.

items.title: Family reported missing took children hiking to limit phone use
items.summary: GERIK: Taking up mountain hiking has been a way for Trans Gerah (Trans GBB) expedition hiker Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin to keep his two children away from excessive mobile phone use. So, I tried hiking," he said. Wan Ahmad Aslam said their hiking initially involved only half-day activities before the family progressed to longer expeditions lasting four, five and six days, with their previous longest expedition lasting eight days.

items.title: Balai Seni Negara, Media Prima explore creative collaboration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Media Prima Bhd today hosted a 14-member delegation from the National Art Gallery at Balai Berita to explore strategic creative collaborations and strengthen communication between the two organisations. Led by the National Art Galley deputy director-general (operations) Rohana Mohd Yusof, the delegation met Media Prima's editorial leadership to discuss ways to connect national art initiatives with wider public audiences. The gallery's representatives also toured Media Prima's broadcast studios, REV Media Group and the newsrooms of The New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd.

items.title: Anwar to chair MA63 meeting on Sabah’s 40pc revenue claim, says Hajiji
items.summary: Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said Sabah would host the meeting, which would also discuss outstanding claims and issues under MA63, Sinar Harian reported. He said this after a working visit to the Kunak Lipids Sdn Bhd Phytonutrient Extraction Plant in Kunak today. However, there are still other matters, including the 40 per cent payment,” he said.

items.title: Presence of Serbian officials at Mladic funeral 'deeply regrettable': EU chiefs
items.summary: BRUSSELS: The presence of Serbian officials at the funeral of war criminal Ratko Mladic was "deeply regrettable", EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa said Tuesday. "The images from Ratko Mladic's funeral yesterday in Belgrade were shocking," European Commission president Von der Leyen and European Council boss Costa wrote online. Serbian Justice Minister Nenad Vujic initially announced "military and state honours" for Mladic, triggering international outrage, before President Aleksandar Vucic tempered the decision.

items.title: Former minister released on MACC bail over Tabung Haji RCI probe, chief commissioner confirms
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — A former minister who was remanded over an investigation linked to the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) was released on Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) bail today. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the release, Sinar Harian reported today. “He (the former minister) has been released on MACC bail,” he said today.

items.title: Should political party donors be protected? Azalina says issue among those being studied
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — If Malaysia were to have a law regulating donations to political parties, should it protect donors from being pursued by anti-corruption investigators after donating money? Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today that this was among the technical issues that have to be studied before steps are taken to introduce a political financing law in Malaysia. she said.

items.title: Zahid: University autonomy must come with accountability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Greater university autonomy must now be accompanied by measurable accountability for the quality of learning and graduate mobility, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. He said the new framework should give universities greater autonomy while maintaining accountability for their performance and outcomes. Zahid said students should be more involved in decision-making and contribute fresh ideas.

items.title: Nazir Razak, Musa Hitam say NEP fostered ‘tongkat culture’ among Malays
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The New Economic Policy (NEP) fostered a culture of dependency among Malays and became too focused on ownership and government assistance, former CIMB Group chairman Tan Sri Nazir Razak and former deputy prime minister Tun Musa Hitam said today. Nazir said the NEP was intended to run for only 20 years and cited former deputy prime minister Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman’s description of it as a 20-year “handicap”. And when it goes on for too long, this ‘tongkat culture’ becomes deeply embedded,” said Nazir, the son of second prime minister Tun Abdul Razak Hussein.

items.title: UiTM student death classified as sudden death pending pathologist report
items.summary: MARAN: The death of a Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) student during an endurance competition last week has been classified as a sudden death pending the pathologist's report, police said. Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal, 21, experienced breathing difficulties during the endurance challenge on Sept 4 before dying at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital in Temerloh the following day. Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said preliminary investigations found no signs of foul play.

items.title: Johor seeks early cloud seeding as Super El Nino looms
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Johor will seek early cloud-seeding operations ahead of the expected onset of severe drought conditions linked to a Super El Nino from October to December, as the state steps up preparations to safeguard its water reserves. State Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said the state government had already engaged the National Disaster Management Agency on preparations for cloud seeding. He said all 17 dams in the state remained under control, although several were being closely monitored for declining water levels.

items.title: Explainer: Where the haze is coming from and how it reaches Malaysia
items.summary: KUCHING: Fires across Indonesia's Borneo and Sumatra islands have fuelled haze in Malaysia and other parts of Southeast Asia, with smoke drifting across borders. The fires pushed air quality to hazardous levels, prompting emergency measures and school closures in Sarawak. The concentration of fires in Kalimantan was particularly significant for Sarawak, as smoke from fires in Indonesian Borneo drifted across the border, affecting areas in southern Sarawak.

items.title: Did the Negeri Sembilan MB sign decree to oust ruler? Claim sees state in renewed palace crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Negeri Sembilan has been thrust again into its unprecedented constitutional crisis, with claims that new Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim allegedly signed a proclamation to depose the state’s ruler, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, just one day after swearing an oath of allegiance to him. According to the statement released by the four chieftains, Ismail met them on August 3 alongside throne contender Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar, the cousin of Tuanku Muhriz and son of the previous ruler. The chieftains alleged that Ismail signed the formal proclamation ousting Tuanku Muhriz during this gathering, paving the way for Tuanku Nadzaruddin’s installation.

items.title: NCT smart industrial park nears 90pct take-up
items.summary: SEPANG: NCT Alliance Bhd has started handing over vacant possession of the first phase of its NCT Smart Industrial Park (NSIP) in South Selangor, with the 280-unit phase already recording a take-up rate of nearly 90 per cent. NCT Alliance executive director Yap Chun Theng said the industrial park will house businesses from various sectors, with a strong focus on technology. The property developer also launched KM2, the second phase of NSIP, marking the next stage of the industrial park's development and expansion.

items.title: Malay Education Mobility Index needed to measure outcomes — Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malay Education Mobility Index should be introduced to measure how effectively education improves the capabilities, skills and social mobility of Malays, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. "The measure of education cannot stop at access, enrolment, qualifications and tuition. The broader measure is how far education develops human capabilities, drives social mobility and strengthens a nation.

items.title: Engineering must drive resilient, regenerative solutions, says UTP chancellor
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Engineering must move beyond solving today's problems and create resilient, regenerative solutions that safeguard future generations, says Universiti Teknologi Petronas (UTP) chancellor Tan Sri Dr Mohd Hassan Marican. He said the role of engineering could no longer be confined to designing systems or developing technologies, particularly amid an unprecedented energy transition, rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and growing global disorder. He said UTP's strategic direction centred on three Grand Challenges: Energy Security, Sustainable Living and Regenerative Futures, which guide its education, research, investments and partnerships.

items.title: Kalimantan forest fires cause severe haze, water shortages
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prolonged forest and peatland fires in South Kalimantan have degraded air quality and caused acute water shortages due to dry weather. Kota Banjar resident and local representative Muhammad Adi Maulana Noor, better known as Adi van der Pijl, said hazy conditions in several areas were severe enough to disrupt daily routines, especially in the mornings. "Conditions here remain dry, well water levels have dropped significantly.

items.title: TH RCI: Former minister released on MACC bail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has released a former minister who was remanded over issues related to the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). The male suspect, in his 60s, was remanded for seven days and released after the remand period expired today. Meanwhile, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter and said the suspect was released on MACC bail.

items.title: Fahmi: Govt agencies to work together to tighten e-commerce rules, curb sale of prohibited goods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Communications Ministry is prepared to work with the Home Ministry, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, police and relevant agencies to strengthen e-commerce regulation and curb the sale of prohibited goods, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said most e-commerce platforms in Malaysia prohibit the sale of prohibited products, including drugs such as fentanyl, but expressed concern that one platform appeared to be too lax in allowing such products to be offered. “The accounts selling these prohibited products may be fake accounts,” he said.

items.title: Low risk of Anak Krakatau volcanic ash reaching Malaysia, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Shifting wind patterns and potential subsequent eruptions could influence the movement of volcanic ash from Indonesia's Mount Anak Krakatau towards Malaysia, though current risk levels remain low. Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said analysis of current wind speed, direction, and volcanic ash monitoring indicates a low probability of the ash reaching Malaysia. "Information from the global Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC) will also enable us to detect any potential ash movement into Malaysian airspace and notify the public promptly."

items.title: Azalina: Malaysians want political funding law before GE16; political parties’ buy-in needed to avoid delay
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysians have voiced their desire for Malaysia to have a political financing law to regulate political parties’ funding before the 16th general election, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today. Azalina’s remarks were based on findings from the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) public engagement sessions. Azalina said the views of political parties would have to be obtained before the proposed political financing law is brought to Parliament, as it would be politicians in Parliament who would vote on whether to introduce such a law.

items.title: Azalina supports tougher scam penalties, but says banks must share responsibility
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said supports the police proposal for heavier penalties, including caning, for online scammers. However, she said efforts to curb online scams should not focus solely on harsher punishment, as financial institutions must also play their part and take greater responsibility. "I have said many times in and outside Parliament that one strategy is for banks receiving scam proceeds to also take responsibility."

items.title: Johor launches week-long operation to capture 5 dogs that mauled toddler
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Johor has launched a week-long operation to track down and capture five stray dogs that mauled a two-year-old girl in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat, on Saturday. State Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khaled said the dogs must be captured and tested for rabies, with the operation to be intensified for at least a week. He said ruling out rabies was crucial not only for the safety of residents but also to ease concerns over Nur Haira Wafiqah Muhammad Hamizi's recovery.

items.title: Civil servants on boards must be active, voice views, says Chief Secretary
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Government-appointed board members must actively strengthen governance and accountability rather than merely attend meetings, said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar. He said civil servants appointed to board positions must play an active role, voice professional views courageously, and evaluate every proposal thoroughly. Shamsul Azri said views, reprimands, or concerns raised by civil servants during board meetings must be recorded clearly in the meeting minutes.

items.title: PM meets smallholders, commodity players to address diesel allocation, infrastructure needs
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: An increased diesel allocation for smallholders, easier access to funding for farm roads, and alternative water sources were among key issues raised during a meeting between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and commodity sector representatives today. Anwar said the engagement also addressed proposals to strengthen smallholder representation in Parliament, alongside functional overlaps between the Malaysian Rubber Board and the Rubber Industry Smallholders Development Authority (Risda). Earlier, Anwar attended a monthly assembly with staff from the Plantation and Commodities Ministry, followed by a closed-door session with Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad alongside smallholders and operators from the rubber, oil palm, cocoa, pepper, kenaf, and timber sectors.

items.title: Boy, 12, tried to rescue sister from five stray dogs
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A 12-year-old boy remains traumatised after witnessing his 2-year-old sister being mauled by five stray dogs in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat, on Saturday. His mother, Nur Wahyuni Harun, 36, said her second child had tried to chase the dogs away after seeing the pack attack Nur Haira Wafiqah Muhammad Hamizi. Nur Wahyuni said Nur Haira had suffered severe injuries, particularly to her head and cheek, besides wounds across much of her body.

items.title: Kwasa Damansara set for population boom, expects 100,000 residents [WATCH]
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Kwasa Land Sdn Bhd expects the population of its 912.57-hectare Kwasa Damansara township to reach about 100,000 within the next five years as more residential projects are completed. Managing director Datuk Adenan Md Yusof said new developments, including almost 2,000 affordable housing units nearing completion and another 4,000 units planned in the next phase, would support the population growth. Phase 2 development, another 4,000 units, is also coming soon by year-end," he said.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng hits PAS over failure to credit him for cutting lottery draws from 22 to eight a year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng has hit back at PAS over what he described as dishonest and hypocritical claims about DAP’s position on Islam, while pointing to his record of reducing special lottery draws when he was finance minister. In a Facebook post, Lim said PAS had failed to acknowledge that he was the first finance minister to reduce the number of special lottery draws from 22 to eight a year when Pakatan Harapan (PH) was in government from 2018 to 2020. “PAS is not honest and sincere when it fails to state that I was the first finance minister to reduce special lottery draws from 22 times to eight times a year during the PH government from 2018 to 2020,” he said.

items.title: Bumiputera education must move beyond quotas towards self-reliance - Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The future of education for the Malay and Bumiputera communities must move beyond quotas towards greater self-reliance and resilience. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the success of the communities should instead be measured by their ability to excel in critical fields such as Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM), develop new technologies and own intellectual property. Zambry said that to achieve this goal, the country's education ecosystem needed to move beyond simply providing access towards improving quality, building competencies, promoting entrepreneurship and advancing from technology use to technology ownership.

items.title: IBS classrooms to ease overcrowding in Melaka schools, says deputy education minister
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 8 — The construction of additional classrooms using the Industrialised Building System (IBS) will enable special rooms currently used as temporary teaching and learning spaces to resume their original functions, said Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh. He said the move would help ease overcrowding while enabling schools to make better use of their existing facilities. “Some schools have had to convert special rooms, including music rooms and laboratories, into classrooms.

items.title: Blocked trails delayed six hikers’ return from Gunung Gerah, says Perak Fire Dept
items.summary: GERIK, 8 Sept — The closure and obstruction of hiking trails that have not been used for a long time were the main reasons why the six hikers took a longer time to make their way before they were found safe last night, after participating in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, on August 29. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the hikers found that the trails at Gunung Beratoh and Gunung Sepat were closed due to these factors. “When they reached Gunung Beratoh and Gunung Sepat, the found that the trails to both these hills were closed as they had not been used by hikers for a long time.

items.title: AirAsia resumes most flights disrupted by Anak Krakatau eruption
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — AirAsia has resumed flights to and from destinations affected by the Anak Krakatau volcanic eruption following the reopening of Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. “With Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport now reopened following its temporary closure since September 6, 2026, AirAsia has resumed affected services to and from Jakarta, with the exception of two flights on September 8, 2026,” it said in a statement today. The two affected flights are QZ178 from Jakarta (CGK) to Bandar Lampung (TKG) and QZ179 from Bandar Lampung to Jakarta.

items.title: Why the Malacca Strait demands a binding Asean security framework
items.summary: The reality was far uglier: London forcibly seized Egypt's fiscal sovereignty, diverted its vast cotton revenues to European bondholders, and transformed a proud civilisation into a debt colony – bled dry so that Lancashire's mills could spin and British shareholders could prosper. If might alone can seize the resources of the weak, then every international contract, every shipping lane, and every digital transaction becomes a hostage to raw force. Over 90,000 vessels transit the Malacca Strait annually, carrying roughly 40 per cent of global maritime trade and nearly 80 per cent of East Asia's oil imports – an annual cargo value exceeding US$5 trillion.

items.title: Perak Fire Dept calls for age limits on children joining high-risk mountain expeditions
items.summary: GERIK, Sept 8 — The Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) recommends that the authorities review the standard operating procedure (SOP) regarding the age limit for children participating in extreme activities and hiking expeditions along challenging routes in mountainous areas. Previously, six climbers who participated in the Trans Gerah Expedition in Gunung Gerah, Kelantan who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing while climbing the mountain on August 29, were safely released from Pos Kemar, 10.20 this morning. The six victims involved, Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, and his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, as well as children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, as well as two mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, were found safe last night before being taken for a health check-up by medical officers at the Post Health Clinic Kemar.

items.title: Police to record statements from six Gunung Gerah hikers after rescue
items.summary: BAGAN SERAI, Sept 8 — Police will record statements from six hikers in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing during the hiking trip. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the six hikers would be taken to the Gerik District Police Headquarters (IPD) for documentation after being brought out from Pos Kemar. Asked whether the couple had committed an offence by bringing their two children on the hiking trip, Mohd Alwi said all four had valid permits.

items.title: Selangor on track to smash RM80bil investment target, eyes RM100bil
items.summary: SEPANG: Selangor is confident of surpassing its RM80 billion investment target this year and potentially setting a new record of more than RM100 billion, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. He said the state had secured RM70 billion in investments by the middle of 2026, putting it on track to exceed the target. Amirudin said Selangor recorded RM33 billion-RM34 billion in investments in the first quarter, before reaching RM70 billion by the second quarter.

items.title: Six Gunung Gerah hikers safely out of forest after days missing
items.summary: “All the victims and the SAR (search and rescue) team arrived safely at Pos Kemar at approximately 9.15pm last night. All the victims underwent a health check-up by medical officers at the Pos Kemar Health Clinic and rested at the facility. Previously, the six victims involved were found safe last night before being taken for a health check-up by medical officers at the Pos Kemar Health Clinic.

items.title: Malaysia plans 9GW of gas-fired power capacity by 2032 as demand rises, says economy minister
items.summary: Akmal Nasrullah said energy demand was showing an upward trend, driven by factors including population growth and higher consumption from energy-intensive sectors such as data centres. “In terms of the projection for energy demand, definitely we see a pattern of increase. Against this backdrop, Akmal Nasrullah said managing energy demand would become as crucial as managing energy supply over the next five to 10 years.

items.title: Selangor on track to top RM100b investment mark this year, says Amirudin
items.summary: SEPANG, Sept 8 — Selangor is confident that the value of investments recorded by the state this year will exceed RM100 billion based on the current positive momentum, said Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. He said the state recorded about RM70 billion in investments up to mid-year, with the investment trend very encouraging. He said the development of new industrial areas, including NSIP in Sepang, as well as the development of a third port on Carey Island, is expected to continue to boost investment activities in Selangor.

items.title: Johor ready for cloud seeding as El Nino looms from October
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 8 — Johor is prepared to conduct cloud seeding exercises if any of the state’s 17 dams experience low water levels in preparation for the El Nino phenomenon by next month, said Johor Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh. “Johor may request formcloud seeding exercises done earlier before the drought period. Mohamad Fazli said Johor’s water levels in all dams are still at a stable level and some are also at a cautionary level.

items.title: Azalina: Politicians could face corruption charges without political financing law
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Politicians could easily find themselves facing corruption cases if there is no political financing law in Malaysia to regulate financial aid given to them, Pengerang MP Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today. “I, personally think as a lawyer, if there is no Political Financing Act, many politicians will be charged with corruption — easy, simple. “Without a clear framework, political financing can open the way to conflict of interest, abuse of power, political corruption and undue influence in the decision-making process,” she said.

items.title: No data centre approval without enough water, power, says Selangor MB
items.summary: SEPANG, Sept 8 — The Selangor government is closely monitoring water and power supply capacity amid the rapid expansion of data centres in the state, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. He said the state would not approve data centre projects without ensuring adequate water and electricity supply, amid growing public concerns over the industry’s resource requirements. Amirudin said every data centre application must obtain approval from the Federal Data Centre Task Force, with power supply requirements to be cleared by Tenaga Nasional Bhd and water supply by Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Anwar urges younger generation to keep Tun Abdul Razak’s legacy, ideas alive in nation-building
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the younger generation not to merely remember the late Tun Abdul Razak Hussein as a historical figure, but instead to rekindle the torch of his struggle and ideas in confronting the challenges of nation-building. Not to bury the ashes of the dead, but to rekindle its flame,” he said when delivering a speech at the Remembering Statesman Tun Abdul Razak: “Architect of Nation-Building” programme at the Tun Abdul Razak Memorial here today. “Statesmen like Tun Abdul Razak were very wise and astute helmsmen.

items.title: Contractor fined RM20,000 after pleading guilty to using fake documents for RM5m Felda project
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 8 — A 50-year-old contractor was fined RM20,000 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of using false documents to obtain a road resurfacing and drainage upgrade project under a Felda scheme worth RM5 million about three years ago. Wan Shahrinizam Wan Ibrahim pleaded guilty to the two charges after they were read to him through an interpreter before Judge N. Kanageswari. The accused paid the fine.

items.title: Sungai Perak blue water caused by rain, minerals and changes in water flow, state assembly told
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 8 — The phenomenon of Sungai Perak turning blue was caused by the interaction of several factors, including increased runoff following heavy rain, the presence of mineral particles and changes in water flow conditions, the Perak State Legislative Assembly was told today. He said the report was presented to the Perak State Executive Council on Aug 19. Teh said Hulu Perak was naturally rich in minerals, while heavy rainfall increased runoff, carrying more mineral particles from catchment areas, particularly open areas, into the river system.

items.title: Anwar says Cabinet consensus provides stability for govt to plan, implement policies
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — Cooperation and consensus among members of the Cabinet are, as a whole, at a good level, thereby contributing to the country’s political stability, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said this had enabled the government to plan and implement the country’s development agenda based on clear policies and a stable political environment. “True, we cannot deny that our performance has been commendable because we have clear policies, political stability and cooperation within the Cabinet, although sometimes on social media it is a little different.

items.title: Zambry: Malay, Bumiputera education must move beyond quotas towards self-reliance, resilience
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The future of education for the Malay and Bumiputera communities must move beyond quotas towards greater self-reliance and resilience. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the success of the communities should instead be measured by their ability to excel in critical fields such as Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM), develop new technologies and own intellectual property. Zambry said that to achieve this goal, the country’s education ecosystem needed to move beyond simply providing access towards improving quality, building competencies, promoting entrepreneurship and advancing from technology use to technology ownership.

items.title: King receives 2026 Auditor-General’s Reports on federal, state finances
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today received and reviewed the 2026 Auditor-General’s Reports on the federal and state governments’ financial management and activities. Sultan Ibrahim was presented with the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2026 on the Federal Government Financial Statements for 2025. He was also presented with the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2026 on the activities of federal ministries and departments, as well as reports covering the financial statements of state governments and agencies, activities of state ministries, departments and agencies, and the management of state government companies.

items.title: Rapid KL says passenger surge behind LRT congestion at Pasar Seni, Kajang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Increased passenger numbers caused congestion at the Kelana Jaya Line interchange at Pasar Seni and the Kajang Line this morning, Rapid KL said. Rapid KL said no schedule delays were reported, while passenger flow and entry controls were being implemented at the affected stations to ensure safety and smooth movement. “As such, to ensure passenger safety and the smooth movement of passengers, entry and passenger flow controls are being implemented at the affected stations,” Rapid KL said in a post on its social media accounts today.

items.title: Anwar: Asean haze mechanism needs stronger action, Malaysia won’t shield firms
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said there was room to improve the existing Asean mechanism for tackling transboundary haze. Anwar was responding to questions on whether the current Asean mechanism on transboundary haze was sufficient and whether stronger enforcement was needed. When asked on action taken against alleged perpetrators, Anwar said those were merely allegations as fires detected were mainly forest fires.
